title: Power Intent Studio: Open-Source UPF/CPF Authoring from GUI — looking for feedback from ASIC/SoC engineers
gist: A SemiWiki forum post announces Power Intent Studio, an open-source GUI tool that elaborates RTL hierarchy (Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL) and lets engineers author or inspect power architecture on it, importing and exporting UPF/CPF. The author seeks feedback and wants to add power-intent validation such as missing isolation detection.

insights.claim: Power intent is hard to understand and maintain when the RTL hierarchy, power architecture and UPF are viewed as separate things.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Pain point that EDA tools for low-power design try to address.
insights.quote: power intent becomes difficult to understand and maintain

insights.claim: Power Intent Studio elaborates the actual RTL hierarchy and lets users create or inspect the power architecture directly on top of it, supporting Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL and Liberty black-box macros.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: An open-source alternative workflow to commercial UPF authoring in EDA.
insights.locator: Power Intent Studio elaborates the actual RTL hierarchy

insights.claim: The tool supports power domains, supply sets, power switches, isolation, retention, level shifters and power states, loads existing UPF onto the RTL hierarchy, and exports UPF or CPF.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Feature coverage spans the core low-power design constructs.

insights.claim: The author plans to explore power-intent validation, such as detecting missing isolation or invalid domain crossings, and invites contributions.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Validation would move the tool toward verification use cases.
insights.locator: I open-sourced Power Intent Studio so others
